title: LoCoMo: Evaluating Very Long-Term Conversational Memory of LLM Agents
core_claim: Very long multi-session conversations expose failures in recall, temporal/causal reasoning, summarization, and multimodal dialogue generation.
memory_operations: retrieve, summarize, reason over event graph
benchmarks: LoCoMo: 10 conversations, 300 turns avg, up to 35 sessions; QA, event summarization, multimodal dialogue generation
baselines: instruction LLMs, long-context LLMs, RAG variants
limitations: mostly generated and then human edited; small number of conversations; not focused on user-agent task action or implicit habits
relevance_to_topic: first strong long-term conversation memory benchmark; good source for temporal event graph design
skeptical_note: still closer to long-context reading/QA than testing whether an assistant learns a user's behavioral defaults

title: LongMemEval: Benchmarking Chat Assistants on Long-Term Interactive Memory
core_claim: Chat-assistant memory should be evaluated over sustained user-assistant histories with information extraction, multi-session reasoning, temporal reasoning, knowledge updates, and abstention.
memory_type: user facts, assistant facts, preferences, temporal updates
memory_operations: online insert, index, retrieve, read, abstain
benchmarks: LongMemEval-S ~115K tokens; LongMemEval-M ~1.5M tokens; 500 curated questions
baselines: commercial memory assistants, long-context LLMs, RAG design variants
limitations: question count is small; preferences are largely explicit facts/preferences; curation still heavily manual
relevance_to_topic: important baseline and closest prior for long user-agent memory QA
skeptical_note: strong systems can optimize retrieval/reading; benchmark does not force learning latent habits from repeated weak evidence

title: MemoryAgentBench: Evaluating Memory in LLM Agents via Incremental Multi-Turn Interactions
core_claim: Memory agents need accurate retrieval, test-time learning, long-range understanding, and selective forgetting under incremental multi-turn input.
memory_operations: incremental insert, retrieve, learn at test time, forget
benchmarks: reconstructed long-context datasets plus EventQA and FactConsolidation; 2071 questions
baselines: long-context agents, RAG agents, agentic memory agents including MemGPT/MIRIX
limitations: broad but less centered on single-user habit understanding; many tasks are transformed from non-personal datasets
relevance_to_topic: shows standard memory agents fail across multiple competencies
skeptical_note: its TTL/procedural tasks are not the same as inferring stable user habits and contextual boundaries

title: LongMemEval-V2: Evaluating Long-Term Agent Memory Toward Experienced Colleagues
core_claim: Agent memory should help agents become experienced operators in specialized web environments.
memory_type: environment experience, workflow, gotchas, dynamic state
memory_operations: insert trajectories, retrieve compact evidence, reader answers
benchmarks: 451 questions, up to 500 multimodal web-agent trajectories and 115M tokens
baselines: RAG slices, RAG+notes, AgentRunbook-R, Codex, AgentRunbook-C
limitations: environment/workflow focus rather than personal user habits; manual question/evidence curation
relevance_to_topic: sets a new standard for ultra-long agent memory and latency-aware metrics
skeptical_note: excellent for environment experience, but not a user-preference/habit benchmark

title: MemoryArena: Benchmarking Agent Memory in Interdependent Multi-Session Agentic Tasks
core_claim: Memory should be evaluated in closed-loop multi-session tasks with causal dependencies between sessions, not just post-hoc recall.
memory_type: task memory, episodic memory, skill traces
memory_operations: store, retrieve, use in later task execution
benchmarks: human-crafted interdependent multi-session agentic tasks across web navigation, planning, web search, formal reasoning
baselines: MemGPT, Mem0, Mem0-g, ReasoningBank, BM25, embedding RAG, MemoRAG, GraphRAG
limitations: less about subjective/user-specific habit inference
relevance_to_topic: important evidence that QA memory benchmarks miss action-dependent memory
skeptical_note: suggests our benchmark should include downstream decisions, not only memory QA

title: BEAM: Beyond a Million Tokens: Benchmarking and Enhancing Long-Term Memory in LLMs
core_claim: Long coherent conversations up to 10M tokens with diverse probes reveal failures of even 1M-context LLMs and RAG as dialogues lengthen.
memory_operations: generate long histories, retrieve, reason, summarize
benchmarks: BEAM: 100 conversations, 2000 validated questions, 100K-10M tokens
limitations: synthetic generation; broad probe categories but not primarily real user habits
relevance_to_topic: shows ultra-long context alone is insufficient
skeptical_note: could be saturated by systems tuned to probes; habit boundary and false-personalization remain underexplored

title: PersonaMem: Know Me, Respond to Me
core_claim: LLMs struggle to use evolving user profiles over up to 60 multi-turn sessions for personalized responses.
benchmarks: 180+ simulated user-LLM histories, 15 scenarios, up to 60 sessions
baselines: frontier LLM direct prompting and memory variants
limitations: simulated personas; evaluates selecting suitable responses more than repeated habit induction
relevance_to_topic: closest prior on evolving personalization
skeptical_note: does not deeply test negative evidence, habit frequency, boundaries, and when not to personalize

title: PersonaMem-v2: Towards Personalized Intelligence via Learning Implicit User Personas and Agentic Memory
core_claim: Implicit user preferences in long multi-session histories remain hard; agentic memory can improve efficiency with a compact per-user memory.
memory_operations: infer, update, maintain compact memory, personalize
benchmarks: 1000 personas, 300+ scenarios, 20000+ preferences, 128K-token contexts
baselines: frontier LLMs, RL-tuned Qwen3-4B, agentic memory
limitations: still synthetic; user preferences are generated from persona specs; less grounded in real interaction logs
relevance_to_topic: strongest close prior for implicit preferences
skeptical_note: a new benchmark must move beyond implicit preference extraction into statistical habit learning and counterfactual boundaries

title: PERMA: Benchmarking Personalized Memory Agents via Event-Driven Preference and Realistic Task Environments
core_claim: Preferences emerge gradually from event relationships; benchmark should model event-driven preference evolution, text variability, and linguistic alignment.
benchmarks: temporally ordered interaction events with MC and interactive tasks
metrics: MC accuracy, interactive task success, fidelity, efficiency
baselines: advanced memory systems vs semantic retrieval
limitations: paper already occupies event-driven preference emergence; need differentiate from it
relevance_to_topic: very close prior; validates that needle-in-haystack preference retrieval is insufficient
skeptical_note: our novelty should target habits as distributional policies with exceptions, not just preference events

title: AlpsBench: Real-Dialogue Memorization and Preference Alignment
core_claim: Real human-LLM dialogues from WildChat can be curated into personalization benchmarks with structured explicit/implicit memories.
benchmarks: 2500 long-term interaction sequences from WildChat with human-verified structured memories
metrics: semantic-matching F1, action-level update accuracy, recall, utilization metrics
limitations: human verification cost; still four lifecycle tasks rather than habit boundary/action evaluation
relevance_to_topic: important data-source precedent for reusing real logs
skeptical_note: if we use WildChat, must avoid duplicating AlpsBench: add longitudinal habit/action tasks and counterfactual non-personalization

title: PAL-Bench / Mem-PAL
core_claim: Service assistants need personalized dialogue memory in long-term user-agent interactions; PAL-Bench provides Chinese multi-session logs and dialogue histories.
benchmarks: PAL-Set Chinese multi-session user logs and dialogue histories
limitations: created with LLM synthesis plus human refinement due to lack of real data
relevance_to_topic: relevant for Chinese service scenarios
skeptical_note: not focused on ultra-long real logs, implicit habits, or false personalization

title: REALTALK: A 21-Day Real-World Dataset for Long-Term Conversation
core_claim: Real 21-day conversations differ from synthetic dialogues; models struggle with persona simulation and long-term memory probing.
benchmarks: 21-day authentic messaging app dialogues
metrics: persona simulation quality, memory probing QA
limitations: human-human messages, not user-assistant task logs; privacy/licensing constraints
relevance_to_topic: source for realistic temporal/emotional variation
skeptical_note: useful for style/noise and stability patterns, but cannot alone evaluate assistant habits

title: WildChat: 1M ChatGPT Interaction Logs in the Wild
core_claim: Opt-in real user-ChatGPT logs provide large-scale timestamped real-world human-LLM interactions.
memory_operations: data source for extracting prompts, patterns, demographics/time
benchmarks: 1M conversations, 2.5M+ turns, timestamped, languages, hashed IP/request headers
metrics: dataset analysis and instruction tuning utility
limitations: raw logs are noisy; user grouping is privacy-sensitive; many users have sparse histories
relevance_to_topic: best scalable seed for real user-agent habit mining
skeptical_note: requires careful privacy filtering and may not contain enough long histories per user unless grouped/stitched

title: LMSYS-Chat-1M
core_claim: 1M real-world conversations with 25 LLMs can support analysis of user prompt diversity and benchmark construction.
memory_operations: data source for prompts and response preferences
benchmarks: 1M conversations from 210K IPs, OpenAI API JSON format
metrics: dataset analysis, moderation, instruction tuning utility
limitations: usually independent conversations; weak continuity across users
relevance_to_topic: source for realistic tasks/domains and distractors
skeptical_note: needs augmentation to become long-horizon memory benchmark

title: MemGPT: Towards LLMs as Operating Systems
core_claim: Virtual context management lets an LLM manage memory tiers for extended chats and document analysis.
memory_type: hierarchical memory, archival memory, working context
benchmarks: document analysis and multi-session chat
limitations: older; limited evaluation by current benchmark standards
relevance_to_topic: canonical baseline for memory systems
skeptical_note: likely weak on latent habits unless explicit memory-write prompts capture them

title: Zep / Graphiti: Temporal Knowledge Graph Architecture for Agent Memory
core_claim: Temporal knowledge graphs improve dynamic enterprise memory over MemGPT and RAG, including DMR and LongMemEval validation.
benchmarks: DMR, LongMemEval
limitations: enterprise/system focus; limited independent benchmark breadth
relevance_to_topic: strong graph-memory baseline for temporal updates
skeptical_note: KG edges encode facts better than distributional habits and negative evidence

title: Mem0: Scalable Long-Term Memory
core_claim: Dynamic extraction, consolidation, retrieval, and graph memory improve LoCoMo performance while reducing latency/cost.
benchmarks: LoCoMo
baselines: six baseline categories incl. RAG, full context, commercial systems
limitations: evaluated heavily on LoCoMo; personalization still mostly fact/preference memory
relevance_to_topic: production-grade baseline for our benchmark
skeptical_note: may store repeated behavior as flat facts and over-apply it without boundaries

title: A-MEM: Agentic Memory for LLM Agents
core_claim: A Zettelkasten-like agentic memory system dynamically creates notes, links, and evolves memory attributes.
benchmarks: multiple model experiments; benchmark details in paper/repo
limitations: agent-driven linking may be costly and judge-dependent
relevance_to_topic: candidate baseline for adaptive organization
skeptical_note: links similarity but may not model frequency, exceptions, or habit confidence

title: SeCom: On Memory Construction and Retrieval for Personalized Conversational Agents
core_claim: Segment-level memory plus compression denoising improves personalized conversation retrieval vs turn/session/summary units.
benchmarks: LoCoMo, Long-MT-Bench+, dialogue segmentation datasets
limitations: improves memory granularity but not a new capability definition
relevance_to_topic: strong construction/retrieval baseline
skeptical_note: better retrieval can still fail if benchmark requires statistical habit inference

title: RMM: Reflective Memory Management for Long-term Personalized Dialogue Agents
core_claim: Prospective and retrospective reflections improve long-term personalized dialogue memory across granularities and retrieval feedback.
memory_operations: summarize at multiple granularities, retrieve, refine using cited evidence
benchmarks: LongMemEval and personalized dialogue benchmarks
limitations: RL/evidence feedback can be prompt/model dependent
relevance_to_topic: strong personalized memory baseline
skeptical_note: reflection may rationalize retrieved facts but lacks explicit uncertainty over habits

title: O-Mem: Omni Memory System for Personalized, Long Horizon, Self-Evolving Agents
core_claim: Active user profiling and hierarchical retrieval improve personalized long-horizon memory on LoCoMo and PersonaMem.
benchmarks: LoCoMo, PersonaMem
baselines: LangMem, A-Mem and other memory frameworks
limitations: profile-centric; benchmark gains do not prove habit boundary understanding
relevance_to_topic: closest method baseline for our proposed benchmark
skeptical_note: active profiling can overfit personas and misread one-off events as stable habits
